name: stork-directory
description: Find, compare and set up MCP servers from Stork's directory. Five read-only tools; no account needed.

interface.shortDescription: Find and set up MCP servers
interface.longDescription:
Stork is a directory of MCP servers. Ask it for a server that fits a task or a product and it returns matching listings: who publishes each one, how it connects, whether it needs a sign-in, and what Stork's last check of its endpoint saw.

What you can do:
- Find an MCP server for a task, for example Stripe payments or browser automation.
- Read one server's listing, including whether its endpoint answered the last check and when its tool definitions last changed.
- Get the configuration to add a server to the editor or agent you use.
- Compare two to five servers side by side.
- Find where a server lives now if you used an old Smithery-hosted address.

Who it is for: developers and teams who build with AI agents and need to choose an MCP server.

Limits: Stork only reads its own directory. It does not install anything, does not run other servers' tools, and does not sign in anywhere for you. A check is one handshake and one request for the tool list, with no account. It does not show that every tool works and it is not a security review. No account is needed.
capabilities: Find an MCP server for a task or product
Read a server's listing and what Stork's last check of its endpoint saw
Get the configuration to add a server to a client
Compare two to five MCP servers side by side
Find where a Smithery-hosted server lives now
defaultPrompt: Find an MCP server for Stripe payments
Compare the Exa and Firecrawl MCP servers
Show me the listing for Notion's MCP server

positive.description: Find a server for a task
positive.prompt: Find an MCP server for Stripe payments
positive.expected_behavior: Returns a short list of matching servers with Stripe's own server first. For each one it says how to connect, whether sign-in is needed and what Stork's last check saw.

positive.prompt: Show me the listing for Notion's MCP server. Did its endpoint answer the last check?
positive.expected_behavior: Finds Notion's own server and returns its listing. Says the endpoint is at mcp.notion.com, that it answered the last check and asks for a sign-in, and gives the date of the check.

positive.description: Get the config for a client
positive.prompt: Give me the config to add Notion's MCP server to Cursor
positive.expected_behavior: Finds Notion's own server, then returns a JSON block for Cursor's mcp.json that points to https://mcp.notion.com/mcp, and says the user signs in to Notion when the client connects. It installs nothing.

positive.prompt: Compare the Exa and Firecrawl MCP servers
positive.expected_behavior: Finds both listings, then shows them side by side: tool names and counts, how each connects, sign-in, licence and repository.

positive.prompt: I was using https://server.smithery.ai/exa/mcp. Where does that server live now?
positive.expected_behavior: Explains that Smithery's hosted addresses stopped on 2026-10-31 and returns Exa's own listing with its endpoint, https://mcp.exa.ai/mcp, and what Stork's last check of it saw.

negative.description: Not about MCP servers. Stork should not be called; ChatGPT answers with its own tools.
negative.prompt: What is the weather in Paris tomorrow?

negative.description: Stork cannot install software or sign in to anything. It may return the configuration for the user to add, and should say the user does the install and the sign-in.
negative.prompt: Install the Notion MCP server on my laptop and sign me in

negative.description: General web search. Stork's search covers only its directory of MCP servers and should not be called.
negative.prompt: Search the web for today's news about OpenAI

publication.release_notes: First release. Five read-only tools that search and read Stork's directory of MCP servers.
